big: A client redeems ₹6.4 lakh from an equity fund bought for ₹5 lakh, eighteen months ago. She asks, 'Do I pay tax on the whole ₹6.4 lakh?' The answer is no. Tax is on the gain, and part of it may be exempt.

lines: I took out ₹6.4 lakh. Is all of that taxed?
Only the gain is taxed, and the gain is the redemption value less the cost of the units sold. Then the holding period and fund type decide the rate.

note: Rates and limits are as per current rules and change with Budgets. Confirm each year.

title: Capital gains on funds
stops: Tax applies to the gain, not the amount redeemed
Equity fund gains within 12 months are long term
Debt-oriented fund gains follow the slab rate
Cess and surcharge are never added
caps: The gain is the redemption value less the cost of units sold.
Within 12 months, equity fund gains are short term.
For specified debt-oriented funds, the slab rate applies.
Cess and surcharge are added on top of the tax.

q: A client redeems an equity fund after 8 months with a gain of ₹40,000. How is the gain treated?
opts: As taxed at her slab rate
why: Long-term treatment needs a holding of more than 12 months.
Within 12 months, the gain is short term and taxed at 20%.
The yearly exemption applies only to long-term gains.
Slab rate applies to specified debt funds, not equity funds.

q: Meena redeems ₹3 lakh of units that cost ₹2.5 lakh. What is the gain?
why: ₹3 lakh is the amount redeemed, not the gain.
₹2.5 lakh is the cost of the units, not the gain.
₹5.5 lakh adds the two figures, which is wrong.
Gain is redemption value less cost: ₹3 lakh less ₹2.5 lakh.

q: A client holds an equity fund for 20 months and has a long-term gain of ₹1 lakh this year. What follows under current rules?
opts: No tax, as it is below the limit
Tax at 20% on the whole gain made
Tax at the slab rate on the gain
Tax on the whole redemption amount
why: Long-term equity gains are exempt up to ₹1.25 lakh a year.
20% is the short-term rate, not the long-term rate.
The slab rate applies to specified debt funds only.
Tax is on the gain and not on the redemption amount.

q: Which fund's gains are taxed at the investor's slab rate, regardless of holding period?
opts: A fund with 70% held in shares
A large-cap index fund, held long
why: Equity-oriented funds have short and long-term rates.
A fund with 70% in shares is equity-oriented. It does not answer what was asked.
For specified debt funds, the slab rate applies at any holding period.
An index fund of large caps is equity-oriented. That does not match this case.

pts: Tax is on the gain: redemption value less the cost of units sold.
Equity funds: 12 months splits short term and long term.
Specified debt funds follow the slab rate. Confirm rates each year.
